findings.title: Move up / Move down read another graph than the Map draws: nothing happens on an unwritten Key slot, an unsent planned Autopsy or another chapter's Remnant, and other nodes jump
findings.what_happens: The Map draws caseGraph(chapter, { chapters, slots: the whole Key plan, autopsy: the chapter's count }) (1146). The button's handler builds caseGraph(chapter) with no options (1929): only the Key slots that have a stored row, no planned Autopsy unless it was sent, this chapter's Remnants only. A node missing from that graph is in no column, so the function returns at 1932, the caller redraws, and nothing is said. A node that is in it is swapped inside the shorter column, and every node of that column gets a manual place while the missing ones get none, so they sink under it. The buttons are drawn on every node and never disabled, at the column's ends too.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM on a fresh chapter presses Move down on "Slot 1" or Move up on the planned Autopsy: nothing moves and nothing is said; presses Move up on the second of two Remnants: both jump over the five slots.
findings.expected: the column as it is drawn (the function's own comment at 1923-1925 says so), and an end-of-column button that says it cannot move
findings.refutation_tried: A slot gets a stored row only when a GM changed it (key-remnants.mjs:199-213; saveKeyPlan skips untouched slots, 830), so a new chapter's five slots have none. onMove hands the handler an id and a step, no graph (1882). nodeEditHtml draws no disabled button (case-map.mjs:285-290). No test measures a move's result: R3661 presses with a stand-in handler, tier 2 "owner-116" presses Move down on a deduction and reads the focus. The pure layout (case-layout.mjs, run alone on node shapes as graphOf builds them): drawn column key:0..key:4 | R1 | R2 | autopsy; the handler's column R1 | R2; Move on key:0 and autopsy: no column; Move up on R1: at the end; Move up on R2 writes R2:0, R1:1 and the drawn column becomes R2 | R1 | key:0..key:4 | autopsy.
findings.probe: game.drpg.investigationDashboard({ view: "map" }) on a chapter whose Key plan nobody wrote; press .drpg-case-edit[data-drpg-edit="key:0"] [data-drpg-case-move="1"] and .drpg-case-edit[data-drpg-edit="autopsy"] [data-drpg-case-move="-1"]; read case-schema.mjs caseRows(chapter).meta (unchanged) and the node order

findings.title: Place on the map and Give a Truth Bullet act on the stored plan, not on the node's fields as typed; a planned Final Truth is placed without them and the typed fields are dropped
findings.control: Place on the map (planned Remnant, planned Final Truth); Give a Truth Bullet
findings.what_happens: The press goes straight to placeIncident, which reads the plan's row from the GMs' store (1905). Nothing writes the node's fields first: a node is written at its Close, at a pick of another node, on leaving the Map and when the window closes, and with every node open (the default since 15.11.2026) there is no Close. So a room, a name or words typed in the node and not yet written are not in the New Remnant or Give window that opens, and a planned Final Truth is placed at once from the stored row: it asks for a room though one is picked in the node, and the Remnant gets none of the typed name, words, visibility or author. Once the plan points at its Remnant the planned node is no longer drawn, so the typed fields leave the window unwritten.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM adds a Planned Final Truth, picks its room, types its name and words and presses Place on the map: asked for the room again, the Final Truth Remnant stands on the map nameless, and the typed words are gone from the window.
findings.expected: the node's fields written first, as a node's Close does (saveOpenNode), or read as typed, as a Key row's Place reads its row (key-remnants.mjs:1315-1318)
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a write before the press: saveOpenNode is called at 1852, 1858, 1863, 2303 and the form is written at the window's close (2431), not at onPlace. The tier 2 tests of the planned kinds set the fields, press the node's Close, close the window and then call placeIncident (tests-tier2.mjs:32030-32037), so the button with unwritten fields is not pressed anywhere. The tooltips say "with every field of this plan filled in" and "in its planned room, or asks for a room first". docs/dev/owner-116/STATUS.md: with every node open the fields are written "when the GM leaves the Map or switches".
findings.probe: Map with every node open; pick "Planned Final Truth" in select[data-drpg-case-add-plan]; set [name="case:<ch>:<id>:room"] and [name="case:<ch>:<id>:label"]; press [data-drpg-case-place="<ch>:<id>"]; read: the window drpg-window-final-room opens, and after placing remnantData(token).public.name is empty

findings.title: On a Map drawn for another chapter, that chapter's Key slot nodes carry the running chapter's slot fields and its Place
findings.control: A Key slot's fields on its node (the group "Slot N"); Place
findings.what_happens: The Map draws the chapter the Table's Chapter filter names. For a chapter that is not the clock's, the graph takes that chapter's stored Key slots (slots: null at 1146), so its Key Remnants and unplaced slots are nodes with a slot number. mapEditors then hangs the Key planner's cells on the node of each slot number, and those cells are built from keyPlan(), which is always the clock's chapter. So under chapter 2's "Slot 1" stand the Name, descriptions, note, Remnant picker, planned room and Place of chapter 3's slot 1; a Save or a close writes them to chapter 3's plan (and onto chapter 3's Remnant where that slot is placed), and Place puts a chapter-3 Key Remnant on the map.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM in chapter 3 sets the Table's Chapter filter to chapter 2 and opens the Map: under chapter 2's first Key Remnant the group "Slot 1" shows an empty name and a Place button; what they type there is saved as chapter 3's first clue.
findings.expected: no Key planner cells on another chapter's nodes, or that chapter's own
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a chapter guard in mapEditors and caseKeyCells: none; the slots are withheld from the graph for another chapter (1146) but the cells are not. Test R3653 compares the Table's and the Map's field names after setting the filter to "Every chapter" (tests-tier1.mjs:9118), where the Map draws the clock's chapter. The overview's Key limit line (mapSummaryEditor:1603) is the clock's chapter's as well.

findings.title: After a redraw a node's planned-minigame rows and its "Ticked: n of m" line are drawn from the store while the select and the boxes hold the GM's unwritten picks
findings.what_happens: Picking a Trial mode shows that mode's rows through a change listener on the window, and a tick updates the folded list's line the same way. Every redraw of the region draws the rows hidden unless the stored mode is theirs, and the line from the stored ticks; live.mjs then puts the GM's unwritten pick back by writing the field's value, which fires no change. So the select reads "Straw Poll" over hidden question and answer rows (what was typed in them is still held, out of sight), and the line reads "Ticked: 0 of 12" over ticked boxes. With every node open nothing writes a node until the GM leaves the Map, so any redraw in between does it: Add deduction, Check consistency, the fold, the order, a player's sheet changing.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM picks Scrum Debate on a deduction, types the question, then presses Add deduction: the first node still reads Scrum Debate but its question and answers are gone from view.
findings.expected: the rows and the line applied from the fields as they stand after a redraw, as wireKeyLimitOverride does for the Key limit (1732-1742, whose comment describes this trap)
findings.refutation_tried: wireMap runs again after every redraw (2416) but its listener is added once and hears change only; nothing reads the selects' values after restore. The fields themselves are carried and written later, so no data is lost; the look is wrong until the mode is picked again or the node is written.

findings.title: On a chapter with no Remnant of its own, one look at the Table sets the Chapter filter to "Every chapter"; the Map then draws every chapter's Remnants and the filter cannot name the running chapter
findings.surface: Investigation - the Table view; the Map view
findings.what_happens: The Map opened first draws the running chapter (the filter is null, read as "this"). The Table's first draw resolves the filter: the running chapter when it has a Remnant, else "" - the same value as a GM's own pick of "Every chapter". mapChapterOf reads "" as every chapter, so after one visit to the Table the Map holds every Remnant of the world beside this chapter's plan. The filter offers only chapters that have a Remnant, so the running chapter cannot be picked to go back; closing and opening the window on the Map is the only way.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM planning chapter 3 before any Remnant of it exists opens Investigation on the Map, looks at the Table and comes back: the evidence column now also holds chapter 1's and 2's Key Remnants, and no filter option removes them.
findings.expected: the Map keeps drawing the running chapter until the GM picks another, and the filter can name the running chapter
findings.refutation_tried: The filter's tooltip says it "picks the chapter the Map draws" and mapChapterOf's comment says a filter of every chapter draws every Remnant: an explicit pick is meant to do this. What is not said anywhere is the window making that pick itself. Key Remnants are reinforced and survive the chapter's sweep (investigation.mjs:951-953), so from the second chapter on there are older ones to draw.

findings.title: Enter in a field presses Save only until the region's first redraw; after it the fields sit in a nested form with no submit button
findings.where: scripts/investigation.mjs:1066 and 1159 (the region's own <form>), 2372-2375 (the contract); scripts/live.mjs:385-390 (toElement)
findings.what_happens: The region's markup wraps its fields in a <form>. At the first render the content is parsed into the dialog's own form, the inner tag is dropped, and Enter in a one-line field presses the first submit button, Save. Every redraw in place parses the same markup in a detached div, where the <form> is kept, and puts it into the dialog: from then on the fields belong to the inner form, which has no submit button and more than one text field, so Enter does nothing. A filter, a node's pick, the view switch or any change of the world is a redraw.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM presses Enter in a Remnant's Name right after opening: the window saves and closes; after changing a filter, Enter in the same field does nothing.
findings.expected: one behaviour of Enter for the life of the window
findings.refutation_tried: A parse check with the harness's jsdom (no module code run): first render 0 inner forms, the field's form is the dialog's; after a replaceWith of the markup parsed in a detached div 1 inner form, the field's form is the inner one, with no submit button. The first half rests on the harness's model of DialogV2 (shim.mjs:1741-1746: the content parsed into the dialog's form); Foundry 14's own first render was not read. The second half is the HTML parser's rule in any browser.

findings.what_happens: A filter or the fold sets the reading and asks for a redraw; neither writes anything first. The owner's rule of 13.11.2026 ("Nie, ma zapisywac", investigation.mjs:1794-1799, 2336) is that a close never loses what was typed; these presses are not a close and lose it earlier. The tier 2 filter test types nothing before it filters.
